# Inline Alert A one-line message that sits in the flow of a form or a section: "That URL ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories'

<Meta of={InlineAlertStories} />

# Inline Alert

A one-line message that sits in the flow of a form or a section: "That
URL is taken", "Changes are saved automatically". No box, no title, no
close button. For a message about a whole page or region, use an
[Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs). Our own spec:
uiguideline.com has no page for it. A plain element.

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Icon** | The variant's filled icon, one line tall. Replaceable, or `false` for none. |
| **Message** | `children`, in the variant's text colour. |
| **Action** | Optional short link or button after the message. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `info` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | `body-sm` or `body`. |
| `icon` | node or `false` | variant's icon | |
| `action` | node | – | |
| `isLive` | boolean | `false` | Announce it when it appears. |

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={InlineAlertStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The whole line is in the variant's text colour.** Alert can keep its
  message in `--foreground` because the box carries the colour; an
  inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is
  4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays
  readable.
- **Alert or Inline Alert?** Alert when the message is about a page or a
  region and may need a title, an action row or dismissing; Inline Alert
  when it is about the thing right above it.

## Usage

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.InAForm} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.LongMessage} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Small} />

For an error on a single field, use the field's own `validationState`
and `helperText`: it is tied to the field with `aria-describedby`. Inline
Alert is for messages about a group of fields or a whole form.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default, read in order with the page.
- `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed
  submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words have to carry the meaning.

# Link Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an outside site...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as LinkStories from './Link.stories'

<Meta of={LinkStories} />

# Link

Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an
outside site. It navigates; it does not act. For an action, use a
[Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/link](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/link).

<Canvas of={LinkStories.InText} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Text** | The link's name. Say where it goes ("See pricing"), not "click here". |
| **Underline** | 1px, thickening to 2px on hover. |
| **External icon** | With `isExternal`: an arrow out of a box, plus "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | string | – | |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary` | `primary` | Colour. `accent` is the foreground. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | – | Omitted, it inherits the size of the text around it. |
| `underline` | `always`, `hover` | `always` | See below. |
| `isExternal` | boolean | `false` | New tab, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, icon and announcement. |
| `isDisabled` | boolean | `false` | Drops `href`, sets `aria-disabled`. |
| `render` | element or function | – | Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link />`. |

Every other `<a>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

<Controls of={LinkStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Underlined by default.** Colour alone does not mark a link for
  someone who cannot tell the colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1), so a link in
  running text keeps its line. `underline="hover"` is for places where
  the context already says "these are links": a nav list, a footer
  column.
- **Hover thickens the line, it does not change the colour.** Every
  variant is a text colour measured at 4.5:1; a hover colour would need
  measuring again for every accent and mode.
- **No `visited` style.** Most links in an app lead to screens, not
  documents, and a purple "seen it" marker there is noise.

## Usage

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Variants} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.UnderlineOnHover} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.External} />

With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props
onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation:

```tsx
<Link render={<RouterLink to="/settings" />}>Settings</Link>
```

## Accessibility

- A real `<a href>`, so it is in the tab order, opens with Enter, and
  shows up in a screen reader's list of links.
- `isExternal` adds "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name: a new
  tab that opens without warning strands people who cannot see it happen.
- `isDisabled` removes `href`, the only thing that stops an `<a>`
  navigating, and marks it `aria-disabled`. Without an `href` it leaves
  the tab order. Prefer hiding a link that cannot be followed, or saying
  in text why it is unavailable.
- Focus shows a 2px `--ring` outline, offset 2px.

# Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories'

<Meta of={MenuStories} />

# Menu

A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an
"Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick
a value for a form, use a Select. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | `trigger`: one button. Menu merges its props onto it. |
| **Popup** | The Select list's surface: `--popover`, border, `--shadow-md`, `--radius-field`, at least 12rem wide. |
| **Item** | Icon (optional), label, shortcut (optional). 32px tall, 44px on touch. |
| **Checkbox / radio item** | A check in the icon column, for both. They do not close the menu. |
| **Submenu trigger** | An item with `items`, and a chevron. |
| **Group label**, **separator** | Structure for longer menus. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | element | – | Required. |
| `items` | `MenuEntry[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `side` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | `bottom` | |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `start` | |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

<Controls of={MenuStories.Default} />

`items` is data, like Select's `options`. Each entry is one of:

| `type` | Fields | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted or `'item'` | `label`, `onSelect`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `isDestructive`, `disabled`, `href`, `items` | `href` makes it a link; `items` makes it a submenu. |
| `'checkbox'` | `label`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `disabled` | |
| `'radio'` | `label`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `options` | One labelled group of radio items. |
| `'group'` | `label`, `items` | A labelled group. |
| `'separator'` | | |

Give a `textValue` when `label` is not plain text, for typeahead.

### Design notes

- **Destructive items use the danger text colour**, on a `--danger-subtle`
  highlight, both at 4.5:1. Put them last, after a separator.
- **Toggles keep the menu open**, so several can be changed in one go;
  actions close it.
- **Shortcuts are display only.** `shortcut` shows "⌘ D"; binding the
  key is up to the page.

## Usage

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Groups} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Submenu} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Links} />

## Accessibility

- The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup
  is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and
  `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and
  `aria-disabled` on disabled items.
- Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows
  move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the
  matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow
  Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names
  the item.

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode, RefObject } from 'react'
import { AlertDialog } from '@base-ui/react/alert-dialog'
import { Dialog } from '@base-ui/react/dialog'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Modal.module.css'

export interface ModalProps {
  /** The button that opens it. Omit when `open` is controlled from elsewhere. */
  trigger?: ReactElement
  /** Required: it names the dialog. */
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  /** Actions, right-aligned under the content: the main one last. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** Max width: 24rem, 32rem, 48rem. Never wider than the screen. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Defaults to `true`, or `false` when `isAlert`. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * A decision that must be made: `role="alertdialog"`, and a click on the
   * backdrop does not close it. Pair it with explicit buttons in `footer`.
   */
  isAlert?: boolean
  /** Close on a click on the backdrop. Ignored when `isAlert`. */
  closeOnBackdropClick?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where focus goes on open. By default, the first focusable element. */
  initialFocus?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  className?: string
}

const widths = { sm: styles.sm, md: styles.md, lg: styles.lg }

export function Modal({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  footer,
  size = 'md',
  hasCloseButton,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  isAlert = false,
  closeOnBackdropClick = true,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  initialFocus,
  className,
}: ModalProps) {
  const showClose = hasCloseButton ?? !isAlert
  const content = (
    <>
      {trigger && (isAlert ? <AlertDialog.Trigger render={trigger} /> : <Dialog.Trigger render={trigger} />)}
      <Dialog.Portal>
        <Dialog.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <Dialog.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <Dialog.Popup initialFocus={initialFocus} className={cn(styles.popup, widths[size], className)}>
            <div className={styles.header}>
              <Dialog.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</Dialog.Title>
              {showClose && (
                <Dialog.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Dialog.Close>
              )}
            </div>
            {description && <Dialog.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</Dialog.Description>}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
            {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </>
  )
  const change = onOpenChange && ((next: boolean) => onOpenChange(next))
  return isAlert ? (
    <AlertDialog.Root open={open} defaultOpen={defaultOpen} onOpenChange={change}>
      {content}
    </AlertDialog.Root>
  ) : (
    <Dialog.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={change}
      disablePointerDismissal={!closeOnBackdropClick}
    >
      {content}
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

/** A button inside the modal that closes it, e.g. "Cancel": `<ModalClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`. */
export const ModalClose = Dialog.Close

# Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories'

<Meta of={ModalStories} />

# Modal

A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a
short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed
and out of reach until it closes. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog)
and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog).

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Backdrop** | A black scrim at 50% over the whole page. |
| **Popup** | `--popover` surface, `--shadow-xl`, `--radius-panel`, 16px padding, centred. |
| **Title** | Required. `heading-sm` (16px), medium. Names the dialog. |
| **Close button** | Top right. On by default, off for `isAlert`. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`. |
| **Body** | `children`. Scrolls when the modal is taller than the screen. |
| **Footer** | Actions, right-aligned, the main one last. Dismiss actions (Cancel) use the `secondary` button. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `trigger` | element | – | Omit when `open` is controlled from elsewhere. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | |
| `footer` | node | – | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Max width 24, 32, 48rem. |
| `hasCloseButton` | boolean | `!isAlert` | |
| `closeLabel` | string | `Close` | |
| `isAlert` | boolean | `false` | `role="alertdialog"`, no backdrop dismissal. |
| `closeOnBackdropClick` | boolean | `true` | Ignored when `isAlert`. |
| `initialFocus` | ref | – | By default, the first focusable element. |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with
`render`: `<ModalClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`.

<Controls of={ModalStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all
  sit at z-index 50. Each portals to the end of `<body>` when it opens,
  so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal lists its
  options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would hide. The
  `WithSelect` story checks it.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.WithSelect} />

- **The body scrolls, not the page.** Title and footer stay on screen
  however long the content is.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Long} />

## Usage

For a decision with consequences, use `isAlert` and say exactly what
will happen in the description. Name the buttons after what they do
("Delete", "Keep project"), not "OK" and "Cancel".

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Alert} />

Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. A Popover suits a
small form tied to one button; an inline message suits information.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described
  by the description.
- Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`,
  and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer
  events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or
  `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its
  own buttons (and Escape).

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Dismissing} />

- The close button is named `Close`, has the 2px focus ring and a 44px
  touch target on coarse pointers.

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { NumberField } from '@base-ui/react/number-field'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './NumberInput.module.css'

export interface NumberInputProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  value?: number | null
  defaultValue?: number
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when the field is emptied. */
  onValueChange?: (value: number | null) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  /** Decimal places shown and accepted. */
  precision?: number
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  name?: string
  placeholder?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function NumberInput({
  ref,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  precision,
  name,
  placeholder,
  disabled,
  required,
  className,
  onValueChange,
  id,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: NumberInputProps) {
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <NumberField.Root
        {...props}
        id={id}
        required={required}
        format={
          precision === undefined
            ? undefined
            : { minimumFractionDigits: precision, maximumFractionDigits: precision }
        }
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next))}
      >
        <NumberField.Group className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.group, styles[size])}>
          <NumberField.Input
            ref={ref}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}
          />
          {/* Base UI names these "Decrease" and "Increase" for assistive tech. */}
          <NumberField.Decrement className={styles.step}>
            <Icon name="minus" />
          </NumberField.Decrement>
          <NumberField.Increment className={styles.step}>
            <Icon name="plus" />
          </NumberField.Increment>
        </NumberField.Group>
      </NumberField.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Number Input A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. Spec: [uiguidelin...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as NumberInputStories from './NumberInput.stories'

<Meta of={NumberInputStories} />

# Number Input

A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/number-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/number-input).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field);
the field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Input** | The number, in tabular figures, formatted to `precision`. |
| **Decrease button** | `minus`. Disabled at `min`. |
| **Increase button** | `plus`. Disabled at `max`. |

Plus the shared **label** and **helper text**.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number or `null` | – | Controlled; `null` is empty. |
| `defaultValue` | number | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`; `null` when emptied. |
| `min`, `max` | number | – | |
| `step` | number | `1` | Buttons and arrow keys. Shift steps by 10, Alt by 0.1. |
| `precision` | number | – | Decimal places shown and accepted. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24, 32px. |
| `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | – | From the shared field. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name`, `placeholder` | string | – | |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required` | boolean | `false` | Native names. |

<Controls of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with a number**, not `onChange`: built on Base UI, it
  takes Base UI's name, and the value arrives parsed rather than as text.
- **`max` is optional with no default.** The spec marks it required with a
  default of 100, which contradicts itself; a quantity with no upper
  bound is common.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added
  from the shared field.

## Usage

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Precision} />

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Sizes} />

Use it for quantities people adjust by a little. For numbers that are
really identifiers — card numbers, postcodes, phone numbers — use a Text
Input with `inputMode="numeric"`: stepping a postcode is meaningless.

## Accessibility

- The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role
  description "Number field"; Up and Down step it, Shift and Alt change
  the step, Home and End go to `min` and `max`.
- The buttons are named Increase and Decrease and are disabled at the
  limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened.
- The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale.
- Stepper buttons widen to 44px on touch screens.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Breadcrumbs, type BreadcrumbItem } from '../../navigation/Breadcrumbs'
import styles from './PageHeading.module.css'

export interface PageHeadingProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'header'>, 'title'> {
  title: ReactNode
  /** One or two lines under the title. */
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Where this page sits. Rendered above the title. */
  breadcrumbs?: BreadcrumbItem[]
  /** Short facts about the page's subject: a status, a date, an owner. Each may start with an icon. */
  meta?: ReactNode[]
  /** Buttons at the end of the title row. They wrap under the title on narrow screens. */
  actions?: ReactNode
  /** A Tabs element under the heading, for sections of the same page. */
  tabs?: ReactNode
  /** The page's own heading is h1; use 2 when the heading sits inside a larger page. */
  headingLevel?: 1 | 2
}

/**
 * The top of a page: where it is, what it is, and what you can do with it.
 * Built from Breadcrumbs and whatever buttons and Tabs you pass in.
 */
export function PageHeading({
  title,
  description,
  breadcrumbs,
  meta,
  actions,
  tabs,
  headingLevel = 1,
  className,
  ...props
}: PageHeadingProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <header className={cn(styles.pageHeading, tabs != null && tabs !== false && styles.withTabs, className)} {...props}>
      {breadcrumbs && <Breadcrumbs items={breadcrumbs} size="sm" className={styles.breadcrumbs} />}
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <div className={styles.text}>
          <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>
          {description && <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p>}
          {meta && meta.length > 0 && (
            <ul className={styles.meta}>
              {meta.map((item, i) => (
                <li key={i}>{item}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          )}
        </div>
        {actions && <div className={styles.actions}>{actions}</div>}
      </div>
      {tabs}
    </header>
  )
}

# Page Heading The top of a page: where it is, what it is, and what you can do with it. Br...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PageHeadingStories from './PageHeading.stories'

<Meta of={PageHeadingStories} />

# Page Heading

The top of a page: where it is, what it is, and what you can do with it.
Breadcrumbs, title, a line of description, a few facts, the page's
actions, and optionally tabs for sections of the same page.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/page-heading.json
```

## Simple

Title, description and the page's main actions. Keep it to one primary
action; everything else is secondary.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With breadcrumbs and meta

A record's page. Breadcrumbs say where it sits; meta holds short facts,
each optionally led by an icon or a Tag for a status. Rarely used actions
go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays short.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithBreadcrumbsAndMeta} />

## With tabs

Sections of the same page as Tabs under the heading. The tab list's line
replaces the heading's own bottom border.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithTabs} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `description` | node | – | Muted, capped at 65 characters a line. |
| `breadcrumbs` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | – | Rendered small, above the title. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode[]` | – | A list of short facts. |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons, a Menu. |
| `tabs` | node | – | A `Tabs` element. |
| `headingLevel` | `1`, `2` | `1` | 2 when the heading sits inside a larger page. |

Every other `<header>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title takes the row
  down to 20rem, then the actions drop underneath it, keeping their order.
  On a phone that means title first, then buttons.

  <Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Narrow} />

- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow, so a record named
  with one long word still fits.

## Accessibility

- The title is the page's `h1` by default. A page has one; pass
  `headingLevel={2}` if the heading sits under another.
- Breadcrumbs are a `nav` named "Breadcrumb", with the current page
  marked `aria-current="page"`.
- Meta is a list, so a screen reader announces how many facts there are.
  Icons in it are decorative; say the fact in words ("12 applicants").
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button.

Pagination

import { useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Pagination.module.css'

export interface PaginationProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children' | 'onChange'> {
  totalPages: number
  /** 1-based. */
  page?: number
  defaultPage?: number
  onPageChange?: (page: number) => void
  /** Pages shown either side of the current one. */
  siblingCount?: number
  /** Pages always shown at each end. */
  boundaryCount?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Render links instead of buttons, for pages with their own URL. */
  getHref?: (page: number) => string
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const range = (from: number, to: number) => Array.from({ length: Math.max(0, to - from + 1) }, (_, i) => from + i)

/** The page numbers to show, with 'start-ellipsis' / 'end-ellipsis' where a run is skipped. */
export function paginationItems(page: number, total: number, siblings = 1, boundary = 1) {
  const start = range(1, Math.min(boundary, total))
  const end = range(Math.max(total - boundary + 1, boundary + 1), total)
  const siblingsStart = Math.max(Math.min(page - siblings, total - boundary - siblings * 2 - 1), boundary + 2)
  const siblingsEnd = Math.min(Math.max(page + siblings, boundary + siblings * 2 + 2), end.length > 0 ? end[0] - 2 : total - 1)
  return [
    ...start,
    ...(siblingsStart > boundary + 2 ? ['start-ellipsis' as const] : boundary + 1 < total - boundary ? [boundary + 1] : []),
    ...range(siblingsStart, siblingsEnd),
    ...(siblingsEnd < total - boundary - 1 ? ['end-ellipsis' as const] : total - boundary > boundary ? [total - boundary] : []),
    ...end,
  ]
}

export function Pagination({
  totalPages,
  page: pageProp,
  defaultPage = 1,
  onPageChange,
  siblingCount = 1,
  boundaryCount = 1,
  size = 'md',
  getHref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Pagination',
  className,
  ...props
}: PaginationProps) {
  const [pageState, setPageState] = useState(defaultPage)
  const total = Math.max(1, totalPages)
  const page = Math.min(Math.max(1, pageProp ?? pageState), total)
  const go = (p: number) => {
    setPageState(p)
    onPageChange?.(p)
  }

  const control = (target: number, label: string, content: ReactNode, extra?: string, current?: boolean) => {
    const disabled = target < 1 || target > total
    const common = {
      className: cn(styles.control, extra, current && styles.current),
      'aria-label': label,
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
    }
    if (getHref) {
      // A link at the ends has nowhere to go: no href, aria-disabled.
      return disabled ? (
        <a {...common} aria-disabled="true">
          {content}
        </a>
      ) : (
        <a {...common} href={getHref(target)} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
          {content}
        </a>
      )
    }
    return (
      <button type="button" {...common} disabled={disabled} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
        {content}
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.pagination, styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      <ul className={styles.list}>
        <li>{control(page - 1, 'Previous page', <Icon name="chevron-left" />, styles.step)}</li>
        {paginationItems(page, total, siblingCount, boundaryCount).map((item) => (
          <li key={item}>
            {typeof item === 'string' ? (
              <span className={styles.ellipsis} aria-hidden="true">
                …
              </span>
            ) : (
              control(item, `Page ${item}`, item, undefined, item === page)
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
        <li>{control(page + 1, 'Next page', <Icon name="chevron-right" />, styles.step)}</li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page nu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories'

<Meta of={PaginationStories} />

# Pagination

Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the
page numbers around the current one. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Middle} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Previous / Next** | Chevron buttons, disabled at either end. |
| **Page** | A square ghost button with the number, tabular figures. |
| **Current page** | The only solid: `--primary` behind `--primary-foreground`. |
| **Ellipsis** | "…" where two or more pages are skipped. Decorative. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `totalPages` | number | – | Required. |
| `page`, `defaultPage`, `onPageChange` | number (1-based) | `1` | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `siblingCount` | number | `1` | Pages shown either side of the current one. |
| `boundaryCount` | number | `1` | Pages always shown at each end. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24 or 32px controls. |
| `getHref` | `(page) => string` | – | Render links instead of buttons. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Pagination` | The landmark's name. |

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page,
total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own.

<Controls of={PaginationStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The width stays put.** First and last page are always shown, the
  current page keeps a sibling each side, and a "…" appears only where
  it hides two or more pages: a single hidden page is shown instead,
  since "…" would take the same room. The number of controls stays the
  same as you move through the middle, so the Next button does not jump.

  <Canvas of={PaginationStories.Ranges} />

- **Links when pages have URLs.** With `getHref` each page is an `<a>`,
  so it can be opened in a new tab and shared; without it, buttons.

## Usage

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.FewPages} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Links} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination", around a list.
- Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has
  `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and
  "Next page", and are disabled (or, as links, lose their `href`) at the
  ends.
- The ellipsis is `aria-hidden`: the page names already say which
  numbers are there.
- Controls are 24px (`sm`) or 32px (`md`), and grow to 44px on coarse
  pointers.

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Popover as BasePopover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Popover.module.css'

export interface PopoverProps {
  /** The element that opens it: one button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  /** Names the popover (it is a dialog). Without one, pass `aria-label`. */
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** A close button in the corner. Escape and a click outside close it either way. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /** Open on hover as well as click, for previews. Content must still be reachable by click and keyboard. */
  openOnHover?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus inside while open, lock page scroll and block clicks outside (Base UI's modal mode). */
  isModal?: boolean
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Popover({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'center',
  hasCloseButton = false,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  openOnHover = false,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: PopoverProps) {
  return (
    <BasePopover.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BasePopover.Trigger render={trigger} openOnHover={openOnHover} />
      <BasePopover.Portal>
        <BasePopover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BasePopover.Popup aria-label={title ? undefined : ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {(title || hasCloseButton) && (
              <div className={styles.header}>
                {title && <BasePopover.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</BasePopover.Title>}
                {hasCloseButton && (
                  <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                    <Icon name="close" />
                  </BasePopover.Close>
                )}
              </div>
            )}
            {/* Base UI only traps focus in a modal popover that contains a
                Close, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. */}
            {isModal && !hasCloseButton && (
              <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={cn(styles.close, styles.hiddenClose)}>
                <Icon name="close" />
              </BasePopover.Close>
            )}
            {description && <BasePopover.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</BasePopover.Description>}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
          </BasePopover.Popup>
        </BasePopover.Positioner>
      </BasePopover.Portal>
    </BasePopover.Root>
  )
}

# Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form,...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={PopoverStories} />

# Popover

A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a
share form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click, stays until
you close it, and holds links, inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must
not. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover).

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Open} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | `trigger`: one button. Popover merges its props onto it. |
| **Popup** | `--popover` surface, 1px `--border`, `--shadow-md`, `--radius-panel`, 16px padding, at most 22rem wide. |
| **Title** | Optional. Names the dialog. |
| **Description** | Optional, `--muted-foreground`. Describes the dialog. |
| **Body** | `children`. |
| **Close button** | Optional, in the corner. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | element | – | Required. |
| `title` | node | – | Or `aria-label` when there is none. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | |
| `side` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | `bottom` | Flips if there is no room. |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `center` | |
| `hasCloseButton` | boolean | `false` | |
| `closeLabel` | string | `Close` | |
| `openOnHover` | boolean | `false` | Also opens on hover, for previews. |
| `isModal` | boolean | `false` | See Accessibility. |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | | | Controlled or uncontrolled. |

<Controls of={PopoverStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Same surface as the Select list.** Popover, Select and Combobox
  popups share the `--popover` colour, border and shadow, and the same
  z-index layer (50); tooltips sit above them at 60.
- **No arrow.** The popup opens 6px from its trigger and lines up with
  it; the gap and alignment already tie it to the trigger.

## Usage

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.ContentOnly} />

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and
  described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-haspopup`.
- Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a click outside closes
  it and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays
  usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped,
  page scroll is locked and clicks outside are blocked.
- Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a
  touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without
  `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus,
  then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible.

  <Canvas of={PopoverStories.Modal} />

- `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content
  stays reachable by keyboard and touch.

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Progress } from '@base-ui/react/progress'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './ProgressBar.module.css'

export interface ProgressBarProps extends Omit<Progress.Root.Props, 'value' | 'children' | 'className' | 'render'> {
  value?: number
  /** The spec's `maxValue`. */
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  isRounded?: boolean
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  /** Progress is happening but how much is unknown: a sliding bar. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Show the value ("70%") after the bar. */
  showValueLabel?: boolean
  /** A visible label above the bar; also its accessible name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function ProgressBar({
  value = 0,
  max = 100,
  size = 'md',
  isRounded = false,
  variant = 'primary',
  isIndeterminate = false,
  showValueLabel = false,
  label,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: ProgressBarProps) {
  return (
    <Progress.Root
      {...props}
      value={isIndeterminate ? null : value}
      max={max}
      aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.root, styles[size], styles[variant], isRounded && styles.rounded, className)}
    >
      {label && <Progress.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</Progress.Label>}
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <Progress.Track className={styles.track}>
          <Progress.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
        </Progress.Track>
        {showValueLabel && !isIndeterminate && <Progress.Value className={styles.value} />}
      </div>
    </Progress.Root>
  )
}

# Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, step...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressBarStories} />

# Progress Bar

Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install,
steps of a setup. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress).

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`, above the bar. Names the progressbar. |
| **Track** | The full length, `--secondary`. |
| **Indicator** | The filled share, coloured by `variant`. A sliding third when indeterminate. |
| **Value label** | `showValueLabel`: the percentage after the bar, in tabular figures. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | `0` | |
| `max` | number | `100` | The spec's `maxValue`. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Track height 4, 8, 12px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary`, `destructive` | `primary` | Colour of the fill. |
| `isRounded` | boolean | `false` | Pill ends on track and fill. |
| `isIndeterminate` | boolean | `false` | Progress with no known amount. |
| `showValueLabel` | boolean | `false` | Hidden while indeterminate. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |

Any other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`, `aria-labelledby`,
`min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`.

<Controls of={ProgressBarStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native
  `<progress>` use.

### Design notes

- **The fill is a text colour, not a solid.** The fill is what carries
  the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the track, and some accent
  solids do not: amber's is about 2.9:1 on white. So `primary` fills with
  `--primary-text`, `accent` with `--foreground`, `secondary` with
  `--muted-foreground` and `destructive` with `--danger-text`, each a
  colour meant to be read as text on the page, which keeps it at 3:1 or
  more on the track.

## Usage

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.ValueLabel} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Sizes} />

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Max} />

When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate
and switch to a value as soon as there is one.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Indeterminate} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--muted-foreground`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops animating between values
  and the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

import { useId, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Fieldset } from '@base-ui/react/fieldset'
import { Radio } from '@base-ui/react/radio'
import { RadioGroup as BaseRadioGroup } from '@base-ui/react/radio-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Radio.module.css'

export interface RadioOption {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface RadioGroupProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>
  options: RadioOption[]
  /** The group's legend. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the whole group; the error message when `validationState` is error. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  name?: string
  /** Colour of the selected radio. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A set of radios, one of which is selected. A radio is meaningless alone —
 * arrow keys move within its group — so the component is the group, with
 * the radios as flat `options`.
 */
export function RadioGroup({
  ref,
  options,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  orientation = 'vertical',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState = 'default',
  className,
  onValueChange,
  ...props
}: RadioGroupProps) {
  // Plain help describes the group once. An error message goes through Field,
  // which puts it on every radio: whichever one has focus, the reader hears
  // what is wrong.
  const helperId = useId()
  const isError = validationState === 'error'
  return (
    <Field.Root
      name={name}
      disabled={disabled}
      invalid={isError}
      className={cn(choiceStyles.field, choiceStyles[validationState], styles.field, className)}
    >
      <Fieldset.Root
        render={
          <BaseRadioGroup
            {...props}
            ref={ref}
            aria-describedby={helperText && !isError ? helperId : undefined}
            required={required}
            onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string))}
          />
        }
        className={cn(styles.group, styles[orientation])}
      >
        {label && (
          <Fieldset.Legend className={styles.legend}>
            {label}
            {required && (
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={choiceStyles.required}>
                *
              </span>
            )}
          </Fieldset.Legend>
        )}
        {options.map((option) => (
          <Field.Item key={option.value} disabled={option.disabled} className={styles.item}>
            <Field.Label className={choiceStyles.label}>
              <Radio.Root
                value={option.value}
                className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.radio, styles[variant])}
              >
                <Radio.Indicator className={styles.dot} />
              </Radio.Root>
              {option.label}
            </Field.Label>
            {option.helperText && (
              <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.optionHelper)}>
                {option.helperText}
              </Field.Description>
            )}
          </Field.Item>
        ))}
      </Fieldset.Root>
      {helperText &&
        (isError ? (
          <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </Field.Description>
        ) : (
          <p id={helperId} className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        ))}
    </Field.Root>
  )
}

# Radio Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. Spec: [uiguidel...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RadioStories from './Radio.stories'

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

# Radio

Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio),
[Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and
[Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset).

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Legend** | `label`: names the group. |
| **Radio** | The 20px circle: `--control-border` outline (darkens on hover), filled with the variant and a dot when selected. |
| **Option label** | Each option's `label`. Clicking it selects the option. |
| **Option helper** | Each option's `helperText`, indented under its label. |
| **Group helper** | `helperText` under the group: the error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

The component is `RadioGroup`.

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{ value, label, helperText?, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `label` | node | – | The legend. |
| `helperText` | node | – | |
| `value` | string | – | Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | string | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `name` | string | – | |
| `variant` | `primary`, `neutral` | `neutral` | |
| `orientation` | `vertical`, `horizontal` | `vertical` | Layout only; arrow keys work either way. |
| `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | |
| `validationState` | `default`, `success`, `error` | `default` | |

<Controls of={RadioStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but
  a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab
  stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props"
  convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components.
- **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's
  `value` says which is checked.
- Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox.

## Usage

Up to about six options. More than that, or options that do not fit on
screen, is a Select.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Horizontal} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Validation} />

## Accessibility

- A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by
  the legend.
- **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or
  the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options
  are skipped.
- Each option's helper text is its own description; the group message
  follows the group.
- The unselected outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page.
- A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on each radio on coarse pointers.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { Theme, type Radius as RadiusPreset } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const COL: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex',
  flexDirection: 'column',
  alignItems: 'center',
  gap: 'var(--space-2)',
}

const STEPS = ['radius-sm', 'radius-md', 'radius-lg', 'radius-xl'] as const

function StepScale() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap}>
      {STEPS.map((token) => (
        <div key={token} style={COL}>
          <div
            style={{
              height: '4rem',
              width: '4rem',
              background: 'var(--primary)',
              borderRadius: `var(--${token})`,
            }}
          />
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const INTENTS = [
  { token: 'radius-control', label: 'control', note: 'Button, badge' },
  { token: 'radius-field', label: 'field', note: 'Input, textarea' },
  { token: 'radius-panel', label: 'panel', note: 'Card, dialog' },
] as const

function Intents() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap}>
      {INTENTS.map(({ token, label, note }) => (
        <div key={token} style={COL}>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              height: '4rem',
              width: '7rem',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'center',
              background: 'var(--secondary)',
              color: 'var(--secondary-foreground)',
              fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
              borderRadius: `var(--${token})`,
            }}
          >
            {label}
          </div>
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
          <span className={docs.caption}>{note}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const PRESETS: RadiusPreset[] = ['none', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'full']

function PresetRow({ preset }: { preset: RadiusPreset }) {
  return (
    <Theme radius={preset} className={docs.stack}>
      <span className={docs.caption}>radius="{preset}"</span>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-3)' }}>
        <Button>Button</Button>
        <div style={{ width: '10rem' }}>
          <TextInput aria-label="Input" placeholder="Input" isFullWidth />
        </div>
        <div
          data-panel
          style={{
            border: '1px solid var(--border)',
            background: 'var(--card)',
            color: 'var(--card-foreground)',
            padding: 'var(--space-2) var(--space-4)',
            fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
          }}
        >
          Panel
        </div>
      </div>
    </Theme>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Radius.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Radius',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Presets: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      {PRESETS.map((preset) => (
        <PresetRow key={preset} preset={preset} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const px = (el: Element) => Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).borderRadius)
    const scopeFor = (preset: string) =>
      canvas.getByText(`radius="${preset}"`).parentElement as HTMLElement
    const parts = (preset: string) => {
      const scope = scopeFor(preset)
      return {
        control: px(scope.querySelector('button')!),
        // The field's corner is on the box that draws it, not the bare <input>.
        field: px(scope.querySelector('input')!.parentElement!),
        panel: px(scope.querySelector('[data-panel]')!),
      }
    }

    // none flattens everything.
    const none = parts('none')
    await expect(none.control).toBe(0)
    await expect(none.field).toBe(0)
    await expect(none.panel).toBe(0)

    const large = parts('large')
    const full = parts('full')

    // full pills the control...
    await expect(full.control).toBeGreaterThan(1000)
    // ...but a field must never reach a pill. The input is 32px tall, so
    // anything at or above 16px is one.
    await expect(full.field).toBeLessThan(16)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeLessThan(1000)
    // ...and it still has to be a step up from large, or "full" would just
    // be "large with a pill button".
    await expect(full.field).toBeGreaterThan(large.field)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeGreaterThan(large.panel)
  },
}

export const Steps: Story = {
  render: () => <StepScale />,
}

export const Intent: Story = {
  render: () => <Intents />,
}

# Radius Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A `radius` pr...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RadiusStories from './Radius.stories'

<Meta of={RadiusStories} />

# Radius

Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A
`radius` preset on `Theme` rescales everything inside it at once, and
components follow because they reference an *intent* — control, field,
panel — rather than a fixed number.

```tsx
<Theme radius="large">
  <Button>Rounder</Button>
</Theme>
```

## Presets

Five: `none`, `small`, **`medium` (the default)**, `large`, `full`. The
default is set by `--radius-factor: 1` and `--radius-full: 0px` on
`:root`, which is exactly what the `medium` preset writes — so a scope
with no `radius` prop and a scope with `radius="medium"` are identical.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Presets} />

Look at the `full` row. **The button becomes a pill; the input and the
panel get rounder but stop short of one.** That is the whole reason this
is a system rather than a number: a fully rounded text field reads as a
search pill in a form that isn't one, and a fully rounded card stops
looking like a container. Only controls opt all the way in.

`none` flattens every corner in the scope to `0`, including panels.

## How it works

Two variables do the work, both on `:root`:

| Variable | Default | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius` | `0.625rem` | you, for the base step |
| `--radius-factor` | `1` | the `radius` preset |
| `--radius-full` | `0px` | the `radius` preset, only at `full` |

Every step is the base multiplied by the factor, so the preset scales the
whole scale rather than replacing it:

| Preset | Factor | `--radius-full` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | `0` | `0px` |
| `small` | `0.5` | `0px` |
| `medium` | `1` | `0px` |
| `large` | `1.5` | `0px` |
| `full` | `1.5` | `9999px` |

The pill is a `max()`. `--radius-control` resolves to
`max(step, var(--radius-full))` — normally the step wins because
`--radius-full` is `0px`, and at the `full` preset the `9999px` wins
instead.

Fields and panels use the same shape with a ceiling wrapped around it:

```css
max(step, min(cap, var(--radius-full)))
```

`min(cap, --radius-full)` is `0px` normally and the cap at `full`, so they
step up with the preset and stop there. Concretely, at the default base:

| Preset | `control` | `field` | `panel` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `small` | 4px | 4px | 7px |
| `medium` | 8px | 8px | 14px |
| `large` | 12px | 12px | 21px |
| `full` | pill | 15px | 27px |

Small (24px) buttons and fields take `--radius-sm` (6px at the default)
instead: the same corner on a box two thirds the height reads as a pill.

The default input is 32px tall, so a pill would be 16px — `field` at
`full` lands under that on purpose, and a test asserts it.

## Intent tokens

What components actually use.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Intent} />

| Token | Used by | Pills at `full` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius-control` | Button, and future badges/chips | yes |
| `--radius-field` | TextInput, and future textareas/selects | no |
| `--radius-panel` | future cards, dialogs, popovers | no |

A new component should pick the intent that matches its shape, not a step.
Getting this wrong is invisible at the default preset and only shows up
when someone sets `radius="full"` — which is exactly the kind of bug a
token system exists to prevent.

## Steps

The raw scale — `--radius-sm` through `--radius-xl` — for anything that is
genuinely decorative rather than a control, field or panel.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Steps} />

These follow the preset like everything else, so a decorative corner in
application code stays in step with the controls beside it.

A genuinely circular element — an avatar, a status dot — should use
`border-radius: 50%` rather than a token. `--radius-full` is the pill
switch, not a "make this round" value: read directly it is `0` at every
preset except `full`.

## Scoping and overriding

Presets nest, and `Theme` takes a `render` prop, so a single component can
opt out without a wrapper element:

```tsx
<Theme radius="full" render={<Button />}>
  Just this one is a pill
</Theme>
```

For a value the presets don't cover, set the variables directly — `tokens`
is applied after the preset, so it wins:

```tsx
<Theme radius="large" tokens={{ 'radius-factor': '2.4' }}>
```

Globally, change the base in CSS and leave the factor to the presets:

```css
:root {
  --radius: 1rem;
}
```

## One caveat about the base

The steps are offsets from the base — `sm` is `base − 4px`, not
`base × 0.6` — so a base far below the default degenerates. At
`--radius: 0.25rem` (4px) the steps are `0 / 2 / 4 / 8px` and `sm`
collapses to a square corner.

The factor does not have this problem, because it multiplies the finished
step. Prefer moving the preset over moving the base, and if the base does
need to change substantially, switch the four `calc()`s in `tokens.css`
from offsets to ratios.

import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Rating.module.css'

export interface RatingProps {
  /** 0 is unrated. Read-only ratings take fractions, e.g. 4.5. */
  value?: number
  defaultValue?: number
  onValueChange?: (value: number) => void
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Shows a rating rather than asking for one. */
  readOnly?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Visible label; the group's name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /** Submitted with a form. */
  name?: string
  /** How each value is spoken, e.g. `(n) => `${n} stars``. */
  getValueText?: (value: number, max: number) => string
  className?: string
}

const defaultText = (value: number, max: number) => `${value} out of ${max} stars`

export function Rating({
  value,
  defaultValue = 0,
  onValueChange,
  max = 5,
  size = 'md',
  readOnly = false,
  disabled = false,
  label,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  name,
  getValueText = defaultText,
  className,
}: RatingProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [state, setState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = Math.min(max, Math.max(0, value ?? state))
  const stars = Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => i + 1)
  const classes = cn(styles.rating, styles[size], className)

  // Read-only: one image with the value as its name; stars can be partly filled.
  if (readOnly) {
    return (
      <span className={classes}>
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
        <span role="img" aria-label={getValueText(current, max)} className={styles.stars}>
          {stars.map((n) => {
            const fill = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, current - (n - 1)))
            return (
              <span key={n} className={styles.star} aria-hidden="true">
                <Icon name="star" className={styles.empty} />
                <span className={styles.fill} style={{ inlineSize: `${fill * 100}%` }}>
                  <Icon name="star-filled" />
                </span>
              </span>
            )
          })}
        </span>
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Interactive: native radios, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the
  // browser's own. Each radio is visually hidden behind its star.
  return (
    <fieldset className={classes} disabled={disabled} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
      {label && <legend className={styles.label}>{label}</legend>}
      <span className={styles.stars}>
        {stars.map((n) => (
          <label key={n} className={cn(styles.star, n <= current && styles.on)}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              className={styles.input}
              name={name ?? id}
              value={n}
              checked={n === Math.round(current)}
              aria-label={getValueText(n, max)}
              onChange={() => {
                setState(n)
                onValueChange?.(n)
              }}
            />
            <Icon name={n <= current ? 'star-filled' : 'star'} />
          </label>
        ))}
      </span>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

# Rating Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's rating, a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RatingStories from './Rating.stories'

<Meta of={RatingStories} />

# Rating

Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's
rating, a difficulty. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating).
Built on native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it.

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | Optional legend over the stars; names the group. |
| **Star** | Filled in `--warning-text` up to the value, outlined in `--control-border` after it. 24px (16px at `sm`, 32px at `lg`). |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | number | `0` | 0 is unrated. |
| `max` | number | `5` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Shows a rating; fractions allowed. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with a form. |
| `getValueText` | `(value, max) => string` | "3 out of 5 stars" | How each value is spoken. |

<Controls of={RatingStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Native radios, not a custom widget.** A rating is "pick one of five",
  which is what a radio group is: arrows, Tab, focus and form
  submission come from the browser, and a screen reader already knows
  how to read it. Each radio sits invisibly over its star.
- **Stars in the bright `--warning` amber.** A rating reads as a
  rating when it looks like one, so the fill is the amber solid, not the
  darker warning text colour. It is 2.1:1 on white, below the 3:1 a
  meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what carries the score: a
  filled star differs from the outlined empty one (`--control-border`,
  3:1) by shape, and the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars".
- **Read-only is one image.** "4.5 out of 5 stars" is one fact, so it is
  read once, and a fraction draws as a star filled part-way.

## Usage

<Canvas of={RatingStories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.CustomText} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Unrated} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

- Interactive: a `<fieldset>` named by its legend, with one radio per
  star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words with
  `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Hover previews the score up to the star under the pointer; focus shows
  the 2px ring around the star.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Stars are 16px at `sm` and grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

import { useRef, useState, type ChangeEvent, type ComponentProps, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Search.module.css'

export interface SearchProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'type' | 'value' | 'defaultValue'> {
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** A visible label. Without one the field is named by `aria-label` ("Search" by default). */
  label?: ReactNode
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
}

export function Search({
  value,
  defaultValue = '',
  label,
  placeholder = 'Search',
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  onChange,
  onKeyDown,
  className,
  ref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: SearchProps) {
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  // Only to know whether to show the clear button; the input stays the
  // source of truth for an uncontrolled field.
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = value ?? uncontrolled
  const canClear = current !== '' && !disabled && !readOnly

  const clear = () => {
    const el = input.current
    if (!el) return
    // Set the value the way typing would, so onChange receives a real event
    // whether the field is controlled or not.
    Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value')!.set!.call(el, '')
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))
    // The button unmounts once the field is empty; hand keyboard focus back
    // to the input rather than losing it. A pointer press never focuses the
    // button (see onMouseDown), so an idle field stays idle.
    if (document.activeElement?.tagName === 'BUTTON') el.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField label={label} disabled={disabled} isFullWidth={isFullWidth} className={className}>
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <span className={inputStyles.affix}>
          <Icon name="search" />
        </span>
        <Field.Control
          {...props}
          ref={(node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
            input.current = node
            assignRef(ref, node)
          }}
          type="search"
          value={value}
          defaultValue={value === undefined ? defaultValue : undefined}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          disabled={disabled}
          readOnly={readOnly}
          aria-label={label ? ariaLabel : (ariaLabel ?? 'Search')}
          onChange={(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            setUncontrolled(event.target.value)
            onChange?.(event)
          }}
          onKeyDown={(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            onKeyDown?.(event)
            // Firefox does not clear a search field on Escape; Chrome and
            // Safari do. Doing it here makes them all agree.
            if (event.key === 'Escape' && canClear && !event.defaultPrevented) {
              event.preventDefault()
              clear()
            }
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}
        />
        {canClear && (
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Clear search"
            className={inputStyles.iconButton}
            // Keep focus where it is: a focused field stays focused, an idle one stays idle.
            onMouseDown={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
            onClick={clear}
          >
            <Icon name="clear" />
          </button>
        )}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Search A field for a search query, with a button to clear it. Spec: [uiguideline.com/com...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SearchStories from './Search.stories'

<Meta of={SearchStories} />

# Search

A field for a search query, with a button to clear it. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search).
The field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Clear} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Search icon** | The `search` icon at the start. Decorative. |
| **Input** | `type="search"`. |
| **Placeholder** | "Search" unless given. |
| **Clear button** | "Clear search", a filled circle-x: shown while there is text, hidden when disabled or read-only. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string | `''` | |
| `onChange` | `(event) => void` | – | Native event, including when cleared. |
| `placeholder` | string | `"Search"` | |
| `label` | node | – | Optional visible label. |
| `aria-label` | string | `"Search"` | Used when there is no `label`. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24, 32px. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | Native. |

<Controls of={SearchStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`label` and `size` are added**, from the shared field,
  so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in.
- **`value` is added** for a controlled query.
- Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Sizes} />

Put the field inside a `<form role="search">` (or `<search>`) when it
searches the site, so it becomes a landmark. The component is only the
field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.

## Accessibility

- `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label
  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event and focus stays in the field.
- The clear button is a real button named "Clear search", with a 44px
  touch target. The browser's own clear control is hidden so there are
  not two.

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Select as BaseSelect } from '@base-ui/react/select'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  popupInset,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export type SelectOption = string | { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }

/** Strings are their own label; objects carry one. */
export function normalizeOptions(options: SelectOption[]) {
  return options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o as ReactNode } : o))
}

export interface SelectProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  options: SelectOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when nothing is selected. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner replaces the chevron. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Select({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: SelectProps) {
  const items = normalizeOptions(options)
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      hasButtonControl
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseSelect.Root
        items={items}
        value={value}
        defaultValue={defaultValue}
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string | null))}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
      >
        <BaseSelect.Trigger
          ref={ref}
          id={id}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
          className={cn(boxClass(size), s.trigger)}
        >
          <BaseSelect.Value className={s.value} placeholder={placeholder} />
          {isLoading ? (
            <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <BaseSelect.Icon className={s.icon}>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" />
            </BaseSelect.Icon>
          )}
        </BaseSelect.Trigger>
        <BaseSelect.Portal>
          {/* Opens below the field like a list, rather than laid over it
              with the selected option aligned to the trigger. */}
          <BaseSelect.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
            <BaseSelect.Popup className={s.popup} style={popupInset(size)}>
              <BaseSelect.List>
                {items.map((item) => (
                  <BaseSelect.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemText>{item.label}</BaseSelect.ItemText>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseSelect.ItemIndicator>
                  </BaseSelect.Item>
                ))}
              </BaseSelect.List>
            </BaseSelect.Popup>
          </BaseSelect.Positioner>
        </BaseSelect.Portal>
      </BaseSelect.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}
