# Radio Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. Spec: [uiguidel...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RadioStories from './Radio.stories'

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

# Radio

Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio),
[Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and
[Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset).

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Legend** | `label`: names the group. |
| **Radio** | The 20px circle: `--control-border` outline (darkens on hover), filled with the variant and a dot when selected. |
| **Option label** | Each option's `label`. Clicking it selects the option. |
| **Option helper** | Each option's `helperText`, indented under its label. |
| **Group helper** | `helperText` under the group: the error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

The component is `RadioGroup`.

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{ value, label, helperText?, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `label` | node | – | The legend. |
| `helperText` | node | – | |
| `value` | string | – | Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | string | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `name` | string | – | |
| `variant` | `primary`, `neutral` | `neutral` | |
| `orientation` | `vertical`, `horizontal` | `vertical` | Layout only; arrow keys work either way. |
| `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | |
| `validationState` | `default`, `success`, `error` | `default` | |

<Controls of={RadioStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but
  a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab
  stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props"
  convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components.
- **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's
  `value` says which is checked.
- Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox.

## Usage

Up to about six options. More than that, or options that do not fit on
screen, is a Select.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Horizontal} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Validation} />

## Accessibility

- A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by
  the legend.
- **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or
  the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options
  are skipped.
- Each option's helper text is its own description; the group message
  follows the group.
- The unselected outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page.
- A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on each radio on coarse pointers.

import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Rating.module.css'

export interface RatingProps {
  /** 0 is unrated. Read-only ratings take fractions, e.g. 4.5. */
  value?: number
  defaultValue?: number
  onValueChange?: (value: number) => void
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Shows a rating rather than asking for one. */
  readOnly?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Visible label; the group's name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /** Submitted with a form. */
  name?: string
  /** How each value is spoken, e.g. `(n) => `${n} stars``. */
  getValueText?: (value: number, max: number) => string
  className?: string
}

const defaultText = (value: number, max: number) => `${value} out of ${max} stars`

export function Rating({
  value,
  defaultValue = 0,
  onValueChange,
  max = 5,
  size = 'md',
  readOnly = false,
  disabled = false,
  label,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  name,
  getValueText = defaultText,
  className,
}: RatingProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [state, setState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = Math.min(max, Math.max(0, value ?? state))
  const stars = Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => i + 1)
  const classes = cn(styles.rating, styles[size], className)

  // Read-only: one image with the value as its name; stars can be partly filled.
  if (readOnly) {
    return (
      <span className={classes}>
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
        <span role="img" aria-label={getValueText(current, max)} className={styles.stars}>
          {stars.map((n) => {
            const fill = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, current - (n - 1)))
            return (
              <span key={n} className={styles.star} aria-hidden="true">
                <Icon name="star" className={styles.empty} />
                <span className={styles.fill} style={{ inlineSize: `${fill * 100}%` }}>
                  <Icon name="star-filled" />
                </span>
              </span>
            )
          })}
        </span>
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Interactive: native radios, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the
  // browser's own. Each radio is visually hidden behind its star.
  return (
    <fieldset className={classes} disabled={disabled} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
      {label && <legend className={styles.label}>{label}</legend>}
      <span className={styles.stars}>
        {stars.map((n) => (
          <label key={n} className={cn(styles.star, n <= current && styles.on)}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              className={styles.input}
              name={name ?? id}
              value={n}
              checked={n === Math.round(current)}
              aria-label={getValueText(n, max)}
              onChange={() => {
                setState(n)
                onValueChange?.(n)
              }}
            />
            <Icon name={n <= current ? 'star-filled' : 'star'} />
          </label>
        ))}
      </span>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

# Rating Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's rating, a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RatingStories from './Rating.stories'

<Meta of={RatingStories} />

# Rating

Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's
rating, a difficulty. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating).
Built on native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it.

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | Optional legend over the stars; names the group. |
| **Star** | Filled in `--warning-text` up to the value, outlined in `--control-border` after it. 24px (16px at `sm`, 32px at `lg`). |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | number | `0` | 0 is unrated. |
| `max` | number | `5` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | |
| `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | Shows a rating; fractions allowed. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with a form. |
| `getValueText` | `(value, max) => string` | "3 out of 5 stars" | How each value is spoken. |

<Controls of={RatingStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Native radios, not a custom widget.** A rating is "pick one of five",
  which is what a radio group is: arrows, Tab, focus and form
  submission come from the browser, and a screen reader already knows
  how to read it. Each radio sits invisibly over its star.
- **Stars in the bright `--warning` amber.** A rating reads as a
  rating when it looks like one, so the fill is the amber solid, not the
  darker warning text colour. It is 2.1:1 on white, below the 3:1 a
  meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what carries the score: a
  filled star differs from the outlined empty one (`--control-border`,
  3:1) by shape, and the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars".
- **Read-only is one image.** "4.5 out of 5 stars" is one fact, so it is
  read once, and a fraction draws as a star filled part-way.

## Usage

<Canvas of={RatingStories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.CustomText} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Unrated} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

- Interactive: a `<fieldset>` named by its legend, with one radio per
  star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words with
  `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Hover previews the score up to the star under the pointer; focus shows
  the 2px ring around the star.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Stars are 16px at `sm` and grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

import { useRef, useState, type ChangeEvent, type ComponentProps, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Search.module.css'

export interface SearchProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'type' | 'value' | 'defaultValue'> {
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** A visible label. Without one the field is named by `aria-label` ("Search" by default). */
  label?: ReactNode
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
}

export function Search({
  value,
  defaultValue = '',
  label,
  placeholder = 'Search',
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  onChange,
  onKeyDown,
  className,
  ref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: SearchProps) {
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  // Only to know whether to show the clear button; the input stays the
  // source of truth for an uncontrolled field.
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = value ?? uncontrolled
  const canClear = current !== '' && !disabled && !readOnly

  const clear = () => {
    const el = input.current
    if (!el) return
    // Set the value the way typing would, so onChange receives a real event
    // whether the field is controlled or not.
    Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value')!.set!.call(el, '')
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))
    // The button unmounts once the field is empty; hand keyboard focus back
    // to the input rather than losing it. A pointer press never focuses the
    // button (see onMouseDown), so an idle field stays idle.
    if (document.activeElement?.tagName === 'BUTTON') el.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField label={label} disabled={disabled} isFullWidth={isFullWidth} className={className}>
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <span className={inputStyles.affix}>
          <Icon name="search" />
        </span>
        <Field.Control
          {...props}
          ref={(node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
            input.current = node
            assignRef(ref, node)
          }}
          type="search"
          value={value}
          defaultValue={value === undefined ? defaultValue : undefined}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          disabled={disabled}
          readOnly={readOnly}
          aria-label={label ? ariaLabel : (ariaLabel ?? 'Search')}
          onChange={(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            setUncontrolled(event.target.value)
            onChange?.(event)
          }}
          onKeyDown={(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            onKeyDown?.(event)
            // Firefox does not clear a search field on Escape; Chrome and
            // Safari do. Doing it here makes them all agree.
            if (event.key === 'Escape' && canClear && !event.defaultPrevented) {
              event.preventDefault()
              clear()
            }
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}
        />
        {canClear && (
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Clear search"
            className={inputStyles.iconButton}
            // Keep focus where it is: a focused field stays focused, an idle one stays idle.
            onMouseDown={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
            onClick={clear}
          >
            <Icon name="clear" />
          </button>
        )}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Search A field for a search query, with a button to clear it. Spec: [uiguideline.com/com...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SearchStories from './Search.stories'

<Meta of={SearchStories} />

# Search

A field for a search query, with a button to clear it. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search).
The field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Clear} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Search icon** | The `search` icon at the start. Decorative. |
| **Input** | `type="search"`. |
| **Placeholder** | "Search" unless given. |
| **Clear button** | "Clear search", a filled circle-x: shown while there is text, hidden when disabled or read-only. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string | `''` | |
| `onChange` | `(event) => void` | – | Native event, including when cleared. |
| `placeholder` | string | `"Search"` | |
| `label` | node | – | Optional visible label. |
| `aria-label` | string | `"Search"` | Used when there is no `label`. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24, 32px. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | Native. |

<Controls of={SearchStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`label` and `size` are added**, from the shared field,
  so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in.
- **`value` is added** for a controlled query.
- Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Sizes} />

Put the field inside a `<form role="search">` (or `<search>`) when it
searches the site, so it becomes a landmark. The component is only the
field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.

## Accessibility

- `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label
  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event and focus stays in the field.
- The clear button is a real button named "Clear search", with a 44px
  touch target. The browser's own clear control is hidden so there are
  not two.

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Select as BaseSelect } from '@base-ui/react/select'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  popupInset,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export type SelectOption = string | { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }

/** Strings are their own label; objects carry one. */
export function normalizeOptions(options: SelectOption[]) {
  return options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o as ReactNode } : o))
}

export interface SelectProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  options: SelectOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when nothing is selected. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner replaces the chevron. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Select({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: SelectProps) {
  const items = normalizeOptions(options)
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      hasButtonControl
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseSelect.Root
        items={items}
        value={value}
        defaultValue={defaultValue}
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string | null))}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
      >
        <BaseSelect.Trigger
          ref={ref}
          id={id}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
          className={cn(boxClass(size), s.trigger)}
        >
          <BaseSelect.Value className={s.value} placeholder={placeholder} />
          {isLoading ? (
            <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <BaseSelect.Icon className={s.icon}>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" />
            </BaseSelect.Icon>
          )}
        </BaseSelect.Trigger>
        <BaseSelect.Portal>
          {/* Opens below the field like a list, rather than laid over it
              with the selected option aligned to the trigger. */}
          <BaseSelect.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
            <BaseSelect.Popup className={s.popup} style={popupInset(size)}>
              <BaseSelect.List>
                {items.map((item) => (
                  <BaseSelect.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemText>{item.label}</BaseSelect.ItemText>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseSelect.ItemIndicator>
                  </BaseSelect.Item>
                ))}
              </BaseSelect.List>
            </BaseSelect.Popup>
          </BaseSelect.Positioner>
        </BaseSelect.Portal>
      </BaseSelect.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Select Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. Spec: [uiguideline.com...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SelectStories from './Select.stories'

<Meta of={SelectStories} />

# Select

Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/select](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/select).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select);
the field is [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | `label`. Clicking it focuses the field without opening it. |
| **Select input** | A button showing the selected label or the placeholder, and a chevron (a spinner while loading). |
| **Options list** | Opens below the field, in a portal. |
| **Option** | Each option, inset by the field's padding so its content starts where the field's text does. The selected one has a check before its label, in the brand colour. Disabled options are dimmed and skipped. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `string[]` or `{ value, label, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. Labels may be nodes. |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | string or `null` | – | |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `placeholder` | string | – | Shown until something is chosen. |
| `label`, `helperText`, `validationState` | | – | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24, 32px. |
| `isLoading` | boolean | `false` | Spinner in place of the chevron; `aria-busy`. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with the form. |
| `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | Native names. |

<Controls of={SelectStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **Outlined only.** The spec's filled, underlined and unstyled appearances were dropped to match the Claude apps, where every select is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with the value**, Base UI's name, instead of
  `onChange`.
- **Native names** for `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`.
- **Options are strings or `{ value, label }` objects.** A bare component
  is not an option: an option needs a value to submit and compare, so a
  component goes in `label`.
- **The list opens below the field** instead of Base UI's default of
  laying it over the trigger with the selected option aligned — the
  anatomy shows a list below.
- **The field keeps its focus ring while the list is open.** Focus moves
  into the list, but the field is still the one being filled.

## Usage

Five to about fifteen options. Fewer: radios, which show every choice at
once. More, or when people know what they want: a
[Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs), which lets them
type.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Sizes} />

## Accessibility

- The field is a button with `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`
  and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` of `option`s.
- **Keyboard:** Space, Enter or Up/Down open it; arrows move, typing
  jumps to a matching option, Enter selects, Escape closes, and focus
  returns to the field.
- **Read-only** locks the value, not the list: it still opens so the
  options can be read, but choosing one changes nothing. The field has
  `aria-readonly`. Use `disabled` when the list should not open at all.
- The label is associated with the field (it is a `<div>` because a
  `<label>` would also click the button).
- The list renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`: it reads the
  root's tokens, so a `Theme` scope around the field does not restyle it.
- Options are 32px, 44px on touch screens.

import { useId, useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Tooltip } from '../overlays/Tooltip'
import styles from './Sidebar.module.css'

export interface SidebarItem {
  type?: 'item'
  label: string
  href?: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A count or short tag after the label, e.g. unread items. */
  badge?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link to="…" />`. */
  render?: ReactElement
}
export interface SidebarGroup {
  type: 'group'
  label: string
  items: SidebarItem[]
}
export type SidebarEntry = SidebarItem | SidebarGroup

export interface SidebarProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  items: SidebarEntry[]
  /** The href of the page the reader is on: that item gets aria-current="page". */
  currentHref?: string
  /** Above the items, e.g. the product name or a workspace switcher. */
  header?: ReactNode
  /** Pinned to the bottom, e.g. the signed-in user. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** An icon rail: labels move into tooltips. Every item needs an icon. */
  isCollapsed?: boolean
  defaultCollapsed?: boolean
  onCollapsedChange?: (collapsed: boolean) => void
  /** Show a button that collapses and expands the sidebar. */
  isCollapsible?: boolean
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

function ItemLink({ item, current, collapsed }: { item: SidebarItem; current: boolean; collapsed: boolean }) {
  // Collapsed hides the badge too, so a count or short tag joins the name.
  const name =
    typeof item.badge === 'string' || typeof item.badge === 'number' ? `${item.label}, ${item.badge}` : item.label
  const link = useRender({
    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: {
      href: item.href,
      className: cn(styles.item, current && styles.current),
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
      // Collapsed, the label is gone from view but must still name the link.
      'aria-label': collapsed ? name : undefined,
      children: (
        <>
          {item.icon && (
            <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
              {item.icon}
            </span>
          )}
          <span className={styles.label}>{item.label}</span>
          {item.badge !== undefined && <span className={styles.badge}>{item.badge}</span>}
        </>
      ),
    },
  })
  return collapsed ? (
    <Tooltip content={name} side="right">
      {link}
    </Tooltip>
  ) : (
    link
  )
}

/** Runs of ungrouped items become one list; groups stay as they are. */
function sections(items: SidebarEntry[]) {
  const out: (SidebarItem[] | SidebarGroup)[] = []
  for (const entry of items) {
    if (entry.type === 'group') out.push(entry)
    else if (Array.isArray(out.at(-1))) (out.at(-1) as SidebarItem[]).push(entry)
    else out.push([entry])
  }
  return out
}

export function Sidebar({
  items,
  currentHref,
  header,
  footer,
  isCollapsed,
  defaultCollapsed = false,
  onCollapsedChange,
  isCollapsible = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Main',
  className,
  ...props
}: SidebarProps) {
  const [collapsedState, setCollapsedState] = useState(defaultCollapsed)
  const collapsed = isCollapsed ?? collapsedState
  const toggle = () => {
    setCollapsedState(!collapsed)
    onCollapsedChange?.(!collapsed)
  }
  const id = useId()
  const list = (entries: SidebarItem[], labelledBy?: string) => (
    <ul className={styles.list} aria-labelledby={labelledBy}>
      {entries.map((item) => (
        <li key={item.href ?? item.label}>
          <ItemLink item={item} current={item.href !== undefined && item.href === currentHref} collapsed={collapsed} />
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.sidebar, collapsed && styles.collapsed, className)} {...props}>
      {(header || isCollapsible) && (
        <div className={styles.header}>
          {header && <div className={styles.headerContent}>{header}</div>}
          {isCollapsible && (
            <button
              type="button"
              className={styles.toggle}
              aria-expanded={!collapsed}
              aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}
              onClick={toggle}
            >
              <Icon name={collapsed ? 'chevron-right' : 'chevron-left'} />
            </button>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <div className={styles.body}>
        {sections(items).map((section, i) =>
          Array.isArray(section) ? (
            <div key={i}>{list(section)}</div>
          ) : (
            // The label names the list ("Projects, list, 3 items") rather
            // than being a heading, so it cannot break the page's outline.
            <div key={i} className={styles.group}>
              <div id={`${id}-group-${i}`} className={styles.groupLabel}>
                {section.label}
              </div>
              {list(section.items, `${id}-group-${i}`)}
            </div>
          ),
        )}
      </div>
      {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
    </nav>
  )
}

# Sidebar The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen: a header, links in named...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SidebarStories from './Sidebar.stories'

<Meta of={SidebarStories} />

# Sidebar

The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen: a header,
links in named groups, and a footer. It can collapse to an icon rail.
Our own spec: uiguideline.com has no page for it. A plain element; the
rail's labels use [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs).

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Header** | Optional: the product name, a workspace switcher. The collapse button sits here. |
| **Item** | 16px icon, label and optional badge, a flush 32px row (44px on touch). |
| **Current item** | A `--selected` fill and medium weight. No accent colour and no edge. |
| **Group** | A small muted label over its items. In the rail, a rule. |
| **Footer** | Optional, pinned to the bottom: the signed-in user, help. Hidden in the rail. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SidebarEntry[]` | – | Required. Items `{ label, href, icon?, badge?, render? }` and groups `{ type: 'group', label, items }`. |
| `currentHref` | string | – | That item gets `aria-current="page"`. |
| `header`, `footer` | node | – | |
| `isCollapsed`, `defaultCollapsed`, `onCollapsedChange` | boolean | `false` | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `isCollapsible` | boolean | `false` | Show the collapse button. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Main` | The landmark's name. |

`render` on an item replaces its `<a>`, e.g. with a router's link. Every
other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={SidebarStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The current page is a fill, not a highlight.** `--selected` sits a
  step past the hover fill (gray-200 against gray-100 in light, white 10%
  in dark), so hover and current never read alike, and medium weight
  carries the state for anyone who cannot tell the fills apart. It stays
  off the accent: where you are is not a call to action.
- **Group names are labels, not headings.** They name their list
  ("Projects, list, 3 items") without adding `<h2>`s that would compete
  with the page's own outline.
- **The rail needs an icon on every item.** Collapsed, the label moves
  into a tooltip on hover and focus, and stays the link's name.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Collapsible} />

<Canvas of={SidebarStories.Plain} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Main". The current item has
  `aria-current="page"`.
- Each group's label names its list through `aria-labelledby`, and
  keeps doing so in the rail, where it is only visually hidden.
- In the rail each link keeps its name through `aria-label`, badge
  included ("Inbox, 12"), and a tooltip shows the same text on hover
  and keyboard focus.
- The collapse button is named "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar"
  and carries `aria-expanded`.

import type { ComponentProps, CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Skeleton.module.css'

export interface SkeletonProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length. */
  width?: string | number
  height?: string | number
  appearance?: 'circle' | 'square' | 'rounded'
  /** Several lines of text: stacked bars, the last one shorter. A circle's rows are rounded bars. */
  rows?: number
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** A gentle pulse. Off by default: many pulsing shapes are noise. */
  hasAnimation?: boolean
}

const length = (v: string | number | undefined) => (typeof v === 'number' ? `${v}px` : v)

/**
 * A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading. Decorative:
 * put `aria-busy` on the region it stands in for, and announce the load
 * elsewhere if it matters.
 */
export function Skeleton({
  width,
  height,
  appearance = 'square',
  rows,
  isFullWidth = false,
  hasAnimation = false,
  className,
  style,
  ...props
}: SkeletonProps) {
  const inlineSize = isFullWidth ? '100%' : length(width)

  if (rows && rows > 1) {
    // Lines of text are bars: a circle would stack into a column of dots.
    const line = cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance === 'circle' ? 'rounded' : appearance], styles.line, hasAnimation && styles.animated)
    return (
      <div aria-hidden="true" className={cn(styles.rows, className)} style={{ inlineSize, ...style } as CSSProperties} {...props}>
        {Array.from({ length: rows }, (_, i) => (
          <div key={i} className={line} style={{ blockSize: length(height) }} />
        ))}
      </div>
    )
  }
  // A circle takes its height from its width, so `height` is ignored.
  const blockSize = appearance === 'circle' ? undefined : length(height)
  return (
    <div
      aria-hidden="true"
      className={cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance], hasAnimation && styles.animated, className)}
      style={{ inlineSize, blockSize, ...style } as CSSProperties}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

# Skeleton A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page keeps ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SkeletonStories from './Skeleton.stories'

<Meta of={SkeletonStories} />

# Skeleton

A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page
keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Bone** | One shape, `--muted`: a line of text, an avatar, an image. |
| **Rows** | With `rows`, a stack of bones with the last one at 60%, like the end of a paragraph. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | number or string | 100% (circle 40px) | A number is px; a string any CSS length. |
| `height` | number or string | 16px | Of each row, with `rows`. Ignored by a single circle. |
| `appearance` | `circle`, `square`, `rounded` | `square` | A circle takes its height from its width; with `rows` it draws rounded bars. |
| `rows` | number | – | Stacked lines, 8px apart. |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Overrides `width`. |
| `hasAnimation` | boolean | `false` | A slow pulse. |

Any other prop goes to the outer `<div>`.

<Controls of={SkeletonStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **`hasAnimation` is off by default.** A screen of pulsing shapes is
  noise; animate the few that matter, or none.
- **`rows` shortens the last line**, which reads as text rather than as a
  block.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Appearances} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Rows} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Animated} />

Match the shapes to the content that will replace them: same sizes,
same gaps. A skeleton that jumps to a different layout on load is worse
than a spinner. For content whose shape is unknown, use a
[Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).

## Accessibility

- **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`. It says nothing to
  a screen reader, so the region it stands in for has to: put
  `aria-busy="true"` on it (as the CardPlaceholder story does) and remove
  it when the content arrives.
- If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a
  Spinner with a label.
- `--muted` is below any contrast floor on purpose. It is not content,
  and should not compete with content that has arrived.
- The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Slider as BaseSlider } from '@base-ui/react/slider'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Slider.module.css'

type Value = number | readonly number[]

export interface SliderProps<V extends Value = number> {
  /** A number for one thumb; an array of two for a range. */
  value?: V
  defaultValue?: V
  /** While dragging. */
  onValueChange?: (value: V) => void
  /** Once, when the pointer is released or a key is let go. Use it for anything expensive. */
  onValueCommitted?: (value: V) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  /** Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrow step. */
  largeStep?: number
  /** Visible label; also the accessible name of a single thumb. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Show the current value (or range) after the label. */
  showValue?: boolean
  /** How the value is written, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`. */
  format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions
  /** One name per thumb for a range, e.g. `['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']`. */
  thumbLabels?: string[]
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  disabled?: boolean
  name?: string
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Slider<V extends Value = number>({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  onValueCommitted,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  largeStep,
  label,
  showValue = false,
  format,
  thumbLabels,
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  disabled = false,
  name,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: SliderProps<V>) {
  const current = value ?? defaultValue ?? (min as V)
  const thumbs = Array.isArray(current) ? current.length : 1
  return (
    <BaseSlider.Root
      value={value as number | number[] | undefined}
      defaultValue={defaultValue as number | number[] | undefined}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as V))}
      onValueCommitted={onValueCommitted && ((v) => onValueCommitted(v as V))}
      min={min}
      max={max}
      step={step}
      largeStep={largeStep}
      format={format}
      orientation={orientation}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      thumbAlignment="edge"
      className={cn(styles.slider, styles[size], styles[orientation], className)}
    >
      {(label || showValue) && (
        <div className={styles.header}>
          {label && <BaseSlider.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</BaseSlider.Label>}
          {showValue && (
            <BaseSlider.Value className={styles.value}>
              {(formatted) => formatted.join(' – ')}
            </BaseSlider.Value>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <BaseSlider.Control className={styles.control}>
        <BaseSlider.Track className={styles.track}>
          <BaseSlider.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
          {Array.from({ length: thumbs }, (_, i) => (
            <BaseSlider.Thumb
              key={i}
              index={i}
              className={styles.thumb}
              // A range needs a name per thumb; a single thumb takes the
              // label, or aria-label when there is none.
              getAriaLabel={thumbLabels ? (index) => thumbLabels[index] ?? '' : label ? undefined : () => ariaLabel ?? ''}
            />
          ))}
        </BaseSlider.Track>
      </BaseSlider.Control>
    </BaseSlider.Root>
  )
}

# Slider Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price range, a b...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SliderStories from './Slider.stories'

<Meta of={SliderStories} />

# Slider

Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price
range, a brush size. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/slider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/slider).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider).

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Range} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Label** | Optional, medium weight. Names a single thumb. |
| **Value** | Optional, after the label: the value or range, formatted, in tabular figures. |
| **Track** | `--secondary`, 6px (4px at `sm`), pill-ended. |
| **Indicator** | The filled part, `--primary-text`. |
| **Thumb** | 20px (16px at `sm`): `--background` with a 2px `--primary-text` ring. One per value. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value`, `defaultValue` | number, or `[number, number]` | `min` | An array makes it a range. |
| `onValueChange` | function | – | While dragging. |
| `onValueCommitted` | function | – | Once, on release. Use it for anything expensive. |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | number | `0`, `100`, `1` | |
| `largeStep` | number | `10` | Page Up / Page Down, Shift+arrows. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `showValue` | boolean | `false` | |
| `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | – | E.g. currency, percent. |
| `thumbLabels` | string[] | – | A name per thumb, for a range. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `name` | string | – | Submitted with a form. |
| `aria-label` | string | – | The name when there is no visible `label`. |

<Controls of={SliderStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **The fill is a text colour**, as on Progress Bar: `--primary-text`
  clears 3:1 on the `--secondary` track for every accent, where the
  solid `--primary` does not.
- **The whole 20px strip is the target**, not just the 6px track: a
  press anywhere along it moves the nearest thumb there.
- **Disabled dims the control, not the words.** The label turns
  `--muted-foreground` and the value stays readable.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Steps} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Disabled} />

A slider is quick but imprecise. When the exact number matters (a price,
a quantity), pair it with a Number Input or use one instead.

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` (a real range input) with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a formatted
  `aria-valuetext`.
- A single thumb is named by `label`, or `aria-label`; a range needs
  `thumbLabels` so each thumb says which end it is.
- Keyboard: arrows move by `step`, Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrows
  by `largeStep`, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`.
- Thumbs keep their 20px size and grow a 44px hit area on coarse
  pointers.

<Canvas of={SliderStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

import { useEffect, useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Spinner.module.css'

export interface SpinnerProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary'
  /** Wait this many milliseconds before showing, so a fast load never flashes a spinner. */
  delay?: number
  /** 0–100. Omit for an indeterminate, spinning indicator. */
  value?: number
  /** Spin even when `value` is given. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Shown under the indicator and used as its accessible name ("Loading" when omitted). */
  label?: string
}

// Circle of radius 10 in a 24-unit viewBox: the stroke scales with the size.
const R = 10
const C = 2 * Math.PI * R

export function Spinner({
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'accent',
  delay = 0,
  value,
  isIndeterminate = false,
  label,
  className,
  ...props
}: SpinnerProps) {
  const [elapsed, setElapsed] = useState(false)
  // Always after mount, even with no delay: the live region below has to be
  // in the page before its text arrives for the text to be announced.
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setElapsed(true), Math.max(0, delay))
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [delay])

  const determinate = value !== undefined && !isIndeterminate
  const clamped = determinate ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value)) : 0
  const name = label || 'Loading'

  const indicator = (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" className={cn(styles.svg, !determinate && styles.spinning)} aria-hidden="true">
      <circle className={styles.track} cx="12" cy="12" r={R} />
      <circle
        className={styles.indicator}
        cx="12"
        cy="12"
        r={R}
        strokeDasharray={C}
        // Indeterminate shows a quarter arc; determinate shows the value.
        strokeDashoffset={determinate ? C * (1 - clamped / 100) : C * 0.75}
      />
    </svg>
  )

  // Determinate: a progressbar that says how far along it is.
  if (determinate) {
    if (delay > 0 && !elapsed) return null
    return (
      <span
        role="progressbar"
        aria-valuenow={clamped}
        aria-valuemin={0}
        aria-valuemax={100}
        aria-label={name}
        className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
        {...props}
      >
        {indicator}
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Indeterminate: a polite live region that is in the page from the first
  // render, empty through the delay. Screen readers announce text inserted
  // into a live region that already exists, not a region that mounts full.
  return (
    <span
      role="status"
      aria-label={name}
      className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {elapsed && (
        <>
          {indicator}
          <span className={label ? styles.label : styles.hiddenLabel}>{name}</span>
        </>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories'

<Meta of={SpinnerStories} />

# Spinner

Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will
take, or, given a value, how far along it is. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner).
A plain element: there is no behaviour here worth Base UI.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Track** | The full circle, `--border`. Frames the motion; decoration. |
| **Indicator** | The arc: a quarter turn spinning, or the value as a share of the ring. Coloured by `variant`. |
| **Label** | `label`, under the indicator. Also the accessible name. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | 16, 24, 32px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `secondary` | `accent` | Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. |
| `label` | string | – | Visible text and accessible name; `"Loading"` when omitted or empty. |
| `delay` | number (ms) | `0` | Renders nothing until it has passed. |
| `value` | 0–100 | – | Turns it into a progress ring. Clamped. |
| `isIndeterminate` | boolean | `false` | Spin even when `value` is given. |

Any other prop goes to the outer `<span>`.

<Controls of={SpinnerStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **`accent` is the default variant**, in `--foreground`: a spinner is
  most often a quiet placeholder inside content that has its own colour.
- **`value`**: A load that can report progress should, and a
  ring reads better than a bar in a small space such as a button or a
  thumbnail.
- **`delay`**: Most loads finish in under half a second; a
  spinner that appears and vanishes in 200ms is a flash, not information.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Determinate} />

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner
only appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Delay} />

For a load of a page region whose shape you know, a
[Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) says more. For
a long task with a known size, use a
[Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).

## Accessibility

- **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by
  `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the
  label, or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once
  `delay` has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region
  that is already in the page, not a region that mounts full.
- **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`,
  `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`.
- The SVG is hidden.
- The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--primary-text`
  (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--muted-foreground`, `--foreground`.
  The track is decoration and may be faint.
- The progress ring's transition stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than
  stopping: a frozen arc reads as "stuck".
- Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the
  spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Card } from '../../data-display/Card'
import { Link } from '../../navigation/Link'
import styles from './Stats.module.css'

export interface StatChange {
  /** As shown, e.g. "12%" or "3.2k". */
  value: string
  direction: 'up' | 'down'
  /** Whether the change is good news. Defaults to up is good; pass it for figures where down is good, like churn. */
  isPositive?: boolean
}

export interface Stat {
  label: string
  value: ReactNode
  /** Context under or beside the value, e.g. "from 71,897". */
  previous?: ReactNode
  change?: StatChange
  /** Shown in a disc before the label. */
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A link at the foot of the card, to where the figure comes from. */
  href?: string
  linkLabel?: string
}

export interface StatsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'section'>, 'title'> {
  stats: Stat[]
  /** A heading above the cards, e.g. "Last 30 days". */
  title?: ReactNode
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3
}

/**
 * Key figures in a row of cards: a label, a value, and optionally the
 * change since last period, an icon and a link to the details.
 */
export function Stats({ stats, title, headingLevel = 2, className, ...props }: StatsProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <section className={cn(styles.stats, className)} {...props}>
      {title && <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>}
      <dl className={styles.grid}>
        {stats.map((stat) => {
          const positive = stat.change ? (stat.change.isPositive ?? stat.change.direction === 'up') : undefined
          return (
            <Card key={stat.label} appearance="outline" size="md" className={cn(styles.card, stat.icon !== undefined && styles.withIcon)}>
              <dt className={styles.label}>
                {/* Inside the dt: a dl's groups may hold only dt and dd. */}
                {stat.icon && (
                  <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                    {stat.icon}
                  </span>
                )}
                {stat.label}
              </dt>
              <dd className={styles.figures}>
                <span className={styles.value}>{stat.value}</span>
                {stat.previous && <span className={styles.previous}>{stat.previous}</span>}
                {stat.change && (
                  <span className={cn(styles.change, positive ? styles.positive : styles.negative)}>
                    <Icon name={stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'chevron-up' : 'chevron-down'} />
                    {/* The arrow and the colour say it at a glance; the words say it to everyone. */}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}>{stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'Increased by' : 'Decreased by'} </span>
                    {stat.change.value}
                  </span>
                )}
              </dd>
              {stat.href && (
                <dd className={styles.footer}>
                  <Link href={stat.href} size="sm" underline="hover">
                    {stat.linkLabel ?? 'View all'}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}> {stat.label}</span>
                  </Link>
                </dd>
              )}
            </Card>
          )
        })}
      </dl>
    </section>
  )
}

# Stats Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and optionally how it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StatsStories from './Stats.stories'

<Meta of={StatsStories} />

# Stats

Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and
optionally how it moved since the last period, an icon, and a link to
the details. The top of a dashboard or a report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stats.json
```

## Simple

<Canvas of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## With trend

`previous` gives the figure to compare against; `change` says by how
much and which way. The colour follows whether the change is good news,
not its direction: pass `isPositive: true` for figures where down is
good, like churn or response time.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithTrend} />

## With icon and link

An icon on a rounded square of the primary colour, and a link at the foot of each
card to where the figure comes from.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithIconAndLink} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `Stat[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `title` | node | – | A heading above the cards. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

Each `Stat` has `label`, `value`, and optionally `previous`, `change`
(`{ value, direction: 'up' \| 'down', isPositive? }`), `icon`, `href` and
`linkLabel` (default "View all").

<Controls of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- As many 14rem columns as fit: three or four on a desktop, one on a
  phone. Cards in a row share a height.

  <Canvas of={StatsStories.Narrow} />

- Figures use tabular numbers, so a row of values lines up digit by digit
  and does not jitter when it updates.

## Accessibility

- A definition list: each figure is the definition of its label, so a
  screen reader reads "Total subscribers, 71,897".
- The change is read as words ("Increased by 12%"), not only shown as an
  arrow and a colour. The colours are `--success-text` and `--danger-text`
  on their subtle surfaces, 4.5:1 in both appearances.
- Each "View all" link carries its figure's label for screen readers
  ("View all Avg. open rate"), so a list of links is not three identical
  entries.
- The icon is decorative.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Stepper.module.css'

export interface StepperStep {
  label: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Override the status worked out from `current`, e.g. to flag a step with an error. */
  status?: 'complete' | 'current' | 'upcoming' | 'error'
}

export interface StepperProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  steps: StepperStep[]
  /** 0-based index of the step the reader is on. Steps before it are complete. */
  current: number
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /**
   * Makes finished steps (and the current one) buttons that go back to
   * them. Upcoming steps stay plain: they cannot be skipped to.
   */
  onStepClick?: (index: number) => void
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const statusText = { complete: 'completed', current: 'current', upcoming: 'not started', error: 'has an error' }

export function Stepper({
  steps,
  current,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  size = 'md',
  onStepClick,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Progress',
  className,
  ...props
}: StepperProps) {
  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.stepper, styles[orientation], styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      <ol className={styles.list}>
        {steps.map((step, i) => {
          const status = step.status ?? (i < current ? 'complete' : i === current ? 'current' : 'upcoming')
          const clickable = onStepClick !== undefined && status !== 'upcoming'
          const marker = (
            <span className={styles.marker} aria-hidden="true">
              {status === 'complete' ? <Icon name="check" /> : status === 'error' ? <Icon name="danger" /> : i + 1}
            </span>
          )
          const text = (
            <span className={styles.text}>
              <span className={styles.label}>
                {step.label}
                {/* Said, not shown: the marker carries it visually. */}
                <span className={styles.srOnly}>, {statusText[status]}</span>
              </span>
              {step.description && <span className={styles.description}>{step.description}</span>}
            </span>
          )
          return (
            <li
              key={i}
              className={cn(styles.step, styles[status])}
              aria-current={status === 'current' ? 'step' : undefined}
            >
              {clickable ? (
                <button type="button" className={styles.target} onClick={() => onStepClick(i)}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </button>
              ) : (
                <span className={styles.target}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </span>
              )}
              {i < steps.length - 1 && <span className={styles.connector} aria-hidden="true" />}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

                  { label: 'Invite', description: 'Add your team' },
                  { label: 'Done' },
                ]}
                current={current}
                onStepClick={setCurrent} />
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
                <Button
                    appearance="outlined"
                    variant="accent"
                    disabled={current === 0}
                    onClick={() => setCurrent(current - 1)}>Back
                              </Button>
                <Button
                    disabled={current === steps.length - 1}
                    onClick={() => setCurrent(current + 1)}>Next
                              </Button>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
};

# Stepper Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up, checkout, a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories'

<Meta of={StepperStories} />

# Stepper

Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up,
checkout, a setup wizard. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper).
A plain element.

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Marker** | A 32px disc (24px at `sm`): a check when complete, the number when current (primary ring) or upcoming (grey ring), a warning icon on error. |
| **Label** | Medium weight; muted for upcoming steps, danger for an error. |
| **Description** | Optional, small, muted. |
| **Connector** | The line to the next step: primary once the step is complete, `--border` ahead. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `{ label, description?, status? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `current` | number (0-based) | – | Required. Earlier steps are complete. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | |
| `onStepClick` | `(index) => void` | – | Makes finished and current steps buttons. |
| `aria-label` | string | `Progress` | The landmark's name. |

A step's `status` (`complete`, `current`, `upcoming`, `error`) overrides
the one worked out from `current`. Every other `<nav>` attribute passes
through.

<Controls of={StepperStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Horizontal puts the text under the marker**, so the connectors run
  marker to marker and every step gets the same width whatever the
  length of its label. Use vertical when the steps have long
  descriptions, or in a narrow sidebar.
- **Only finished steps can be revisited.** With `onStepClick`, complete
  and current steps become buttons; upcoming ones stay text, because a
  flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs.
- **Complete is filled, current is ringed.** Both use the primary
  colour; the fill says "done", the ring says "you are here".

## Usage

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Navigable} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.WithError} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Small} />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen
  readers announce the number of steps and the position of each.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in
  visually hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started",
  "Workspace, has an error".
- With `onStepClick`, the clickable steps are real buttons with the
  focus ring, and grow to 44px on coarse pointers.

<Meta of={SuccessStateStories} />

# Success State

What a flow shows when it has finished: the invites are sent, the import
is done, the inbox is empty. It confirms what happened and offers the
next step. Our own spec: uiguideline.com has no page for it. Built on
[Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs), in the
success tone.

<Canvas of={SuccessStateStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

Empty State's parts, with the icon disc in `--success-subtle` behind the
`success` icon in `--success-text`.

## Props

Every Empty State prop (`icon`, `title`, `description`, `action`,
`size`, `headingLevel`), and:

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `isLive` | boolean | `false` | `role="status"`. |

<Controls of={SuccessStateStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **A success state ends a flow; a Toast confirms an action.** Use this
  when the screen the reader was on is finished (a sent form, a completed
  import) and needs replacing. For a quick "Saved" that leaves the screen
  as it was, use a Toast.
- **Lead with the next step.** The action is where the reader goes now.

## Usage

<Canvas of={SuccessStateStories.Small} />

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading, as on Empty State.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="status"`, read politely when it replaces a
  form or a progress view.

# Switch Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately. Spec: [uiguideline.com/comp...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SwitchStories from './Switch.stories'

<Meta of={SwitchStories} />

# Switch

Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch)
and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field).

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Variants} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Track** | The pill. `--control-border` when off, the variant's solid when on. |
| **Thumb** | Slides to the end when on. The page colour off, the variant's label colour on. |
| **Label** | `label`. Clicking it toggles the switch. |
| **Helper text** | `helperText`, indented under the label. The error message when `validationState` is error. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | boolean | – | Controlled. |
| `defaultChecked` | boolean | `false` | The spec's `defaultValue`. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked) => void` | – | The spec's `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | – | |
| `helperText` | node | – | Not in the spec's list; see below. |
| `name` | string | – | |
| `value` | string | `"on"` | Submitted under `name` when on. |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` | Track 28×16, 36×20, 44×24px. |
| `variant` | `primary`, `accent`, `destructive` | `primary` | Colour of the on state. |
| `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` | boolean | `false` | |
| `validationState` | `default`, `success`, `error` | `default` | |

<Controls of={SwitchStories.Default} />

### Differences from the spec

- **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for
  the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to
  say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message.

## Usage

A switch acts at once, like a light switch. If the choice only applies
when a form is submitted, use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Validation} />

## Accessibility

- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it. The label wraps
  the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it.
- The off track is `--control-border`, measured at 3:1 on the page on
  every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both
  states.
- `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the
  error state the switch has `aria-invalid`.
- A hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carries `name`, `value` and
  `required` into native form submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers; the thumb stops animating
  under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import styles from './DataTablePage.module.css'

const focusable =
  'input:not([disabled]):not([type="hidden"]), button:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), a[href], [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'

export interface TableToolbarProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  /** Search, filters and the primary action. Shown while nothing is selected. */
  children: ReactNode
  /** How many rows are selected. From 1 up, the toolbar shows the selection's actions instead. */
  selectedCount?: number
  /** Actions for the selected rows, e.g. Archive and Delete. */
  selectionActions?: ReactNode
  onClearSelection?: () => void
  /** Defaults to "{n} selected". */
  selectionLabel?: (count: number) => string
}

/**
 * The bar above a table: search, filters and the page's main action; while
 * rows are selected, what you can do with them instead.
 */
export function TableToolbar({
  children,
  selectedCount = 0,
  selectionActions,
  onClearSelection,
  selectionLabel = (n) => `${n} selected`,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: TableToolbarProps) {
  const selecting = selectedCount > 0
  const toolbarRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const wasSelecting = useRef(selecting)
  // Archive or Clear selection unmounts the button that had focus, which
  // drops it on the body. Pick it up in the tools that came back instead.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const toolbar = toolbarRef.current
    if (wasSelecting.current && !selecting && toolbar) {
      const active = document.activeElement
      if (!active || active === document.body || !active.isConnected) {
        const first = toolbar.querySelector<HTMLElement>(focusable)
        if (first) first.focus()
        else {
          toolbar.tabIndex = -1
          toolbar.focus()
        }
      }
    }
    wasSelecting.current = selecting
  }, [selecting])
  return (
    <div
      ref={(node) => {
        toolbarRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.toolbar, selecting && styles.selecting, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {/* Always in the page, so the count is announced as it changes. */}
      <p role="status" className={selecting ? styles.count : styles.srOnly}>
        {selecting ? selectionLabel(selectedCount) : ''}
      </p>
      {selecting ? (
        <div className={styles.selectionActions}>
          {selectionActions}
          {onClearSelection && (
            <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" size="sm" onClick={onClearSelection}>
              Clear selection
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>
      ) : (
        children
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** Put the filters' flexible part here: it takes the free space and wraps first. */
export function TableToolbarGroup({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props} />
}

export interface TableFooterProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  /** E.g. "Showing 1–10 of 57". */
  summary?: ReactNode
  /** Usually Pagination. */
  children?: ReactNode
}

/** The bar under a table: what is shown, and the pages. */
export function TableFooter({ summary, children, className, ...props }: TableFooterProps) {
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.footer, className)} {...props}>
      {summary && <p className={styles.summary}>{summary}</p>}
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}

# Data Table Page A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DataTablePageStories from './DataTablePage.stories'

<Meta of={DataTablePageStories} />

# Data Table Page

A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs),
what is shown and the pages below it, and, while rows are selected, what
you can do with them. Two pieces, `TableToolbar` (with
`TableToolbarGroup`) and `TableFooter`, around the kit's Table, Search,
Select and Pagination. Filtering, paging and the data are yours: the
stories show one way to wire them.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/data-table-page.json
```

## Toolbar and pagination

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.ToolbarAndPagination} />

## Bulk actions

With `selectedCount` above zero the toolbar swaps its tools for the
selection's actions and a "Clear selection" button, on the accent
surface so the change of mode is visible.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.BulkActions} />

## Empty result

When nothing matches, the Table's `emptyState` says so and offers the way
back; the footer goes away.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.EmptyResult} />

## Props

**TableToolbar**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | Search, filters, the primary action. |
| `selectedCount` | number | `0` | From 1, the selection bar replaces the children. |
| `selectionActions` | node | – | |
| `onClearSelection` | function | – | Shows "Clear selection". |
| `selectionLabel` | `(n) => string` | `"{n} selected"` | |

`TableToolbarGroup` wraps the part that should take the free space and
wrap first, usually the search and filters.

**TableFooter** takes `summary` ("Showing 1–5 of 12") and, as children,
usually a Pagination.

## Behaviour to copy

- **Filtering returns to page 1.** A new query on page 3 would otherwise
  show an empty page, or a page the reader never asked for.
- **Selection is by id**, so it survives sorting and paging (Table's
  `getRowId`), and an action clears it once it has been applied.
- Both bars wrap: on a phone the search takes its own line and the
  filters and action flow under it.

## Accessibility

- The selection count is a polite status line that is always in the page,
  so "2 selected" is announced as it changes, and silence when it clears.
- Search and the status filter are named ("Search projects", "Status")
  without visible labels, since the table's caption and placeholder make
  their purpose clear on screen.
- The empty state is a heading inside the table's body, so a screen reader
  reaching the table hears why it is empty.

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Tabs as BaseTabs } from '@base-ui/react/tabs'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tabs.module.css'

export interface TabItem {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  /** The panel shown while this tab is selected. */
  content?: ReactNode
  icon?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface TabsProps {
  items: TabItem[]
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** `underline`: a line under the selected tab. `pills`: a filled segment, for switching views in a toolbar. */
  appearance?: 'underline' | 'pills'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Tabs share the full width equally. */
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Select a tab as soon as it gets focus, rather than on Enter or Space. */
  activateOnFocus?: boolean
  /** Keep hidden panels in the DOM, e.g. to preserve their state. */
  keepMounted?: boolean
  /** Names the tab list when nothing on the page does. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Tabs({
  items,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  appearance = 'underline',
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  isFullWidth = false,
  activateOnFocus = false,
  keepMounted = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: TabsProps) {
  return (
    <BaseTabs.Root
      value={value}
      defaultValue={defaultValue ?? (value === undefined ? items.find((i) => !i.disabled)?.value : undefined)}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as string))}
      orientation={orientation}
      className={cn(styles.tabs, styles[appearance], styles[size], styles[orientation], isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, className)}
    >
      <BaseTabs.List className={styles.list} activateOnFocus={activateOnFocus} aria-label={ariaLabel}>
        {items.map((item) => (
          <BaseTabs.Tab key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={styles.tab}>
            {item.icon && (
              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                {item.icon}
              </span>
            )}
            {item.label}
          </BaseTabs.Tab>
        ))}
        <BaseTabs.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
      </BaseTabs.List>
      {items.map(
        (item) =>
          item.content !== undefined && (
            <BaseTabs.Panel key={item.value} value={item.value} keepMounted={keepMounted} className={styles.panel}>
              {item.content}
            </BaseTabs.Panel>
          ),
      )}
    </BaseTabs.Root>
  )
}

# Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activi...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories'

<Meta of={TabsStories} />

# Tabs

Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page:
Overview, Activity, Settings of one project. Spec:
[uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs).
Behaviour from Base UI's [Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs).

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Tab list** | The row (or column) of tabs. |
| **Tab** | Optional icon and a label, medium weight. `--muted-foreground` until selected, then `--primary-text` (underline) or `--foreground` (pills; `--subtle-foreground` until selected). |
| **Indicator** | `underline`: a 2px `--primary` bar that slides to the selected tab. `pills`: a `--card` chip with a `--border` hairline and `--shadow-xs` on a `--muted` track. |
| **Panel** | The selected tab's `content`. |

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ value, label, content?, icon?, disabled? }[]` | – | Required. |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | string | first enabled | Controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `appearance` | `underline`, `pills` | `underline` | |
| `size` | `sm`, `md` | `md` | 24 or 32px tabs. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | |
| `isFullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Tabs share the width equally. |
| `activateOnFocus` | boolean | `false` | Select as focus moves. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keep hidden panels in the DOM. |
| `aria-label` | string | – | Names the tab list. |

<Controls of={TabsStories.Default} />

### Design notes

- **Underline for sections, pills for view switches.** Underline tabs
  sit on a 1px rule and read as the sections of a page; pills sit in a
  `--muted` track and suit a compact "List / Board" switch in a toolbar.
- **Pills keep full-strength labels.** `--muted-foreground` is 4.3:1 on
  the `--muted` track, under the 4.5:1 floor, so every pill label is
  `--foreground` and the selected one is marked by its lifted,
  outlined segment rather than by colour.
- **Selection is manual by default.** Arrow keys move focus; Enter or
  Space selects. That keeps a slow panel from loading on every keypress;
  `activateOnFocus` switches to selecting as you go, for light panels.

## Usage

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Pills} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.FullWidth} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.WithIcons} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Small} />

## Accessibility

- `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and
  `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab.
  Name the list with `aria-label` when no heading does.
- One tab stop: Tab moves into the list and out to the panel; arrows
  move between tabs (Up and Down when vertical), Home and End jump to
  the ends.
- A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is
  found and announced, but it cannot be selected.
- Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on coarse pointers.
